headline: Minneapolis council members will try today to overrule the mayor's veto of a rule that would put a human safety monitor in every driverless taxi.
score_reason: Pending vote with national interest as a possible first-in-US rule; outcome unknown.
importance_line: Waymo and ride-hail drivers in Minneapolis are affected, as the vote may make the city the first in the US to require a person inside driverless taxis, but the council may not have the nine votes needed.
summary: FOX 9 reports that the Minneapolis City Council, which voted 7-6 on 1 Oct 2026 to require a licensed human safety monitor inside driverless rideshare cars, is due to vote on 15 Oct on overriding Mayor Jacob Frey's veto, which needs nine votes. St. Paul's council chose on 14 Oct to study driverless vehicles instead, and Waymo has called the Minneapolis rule a 'de-facto ban'.
